business: SpeakCheck — iPhone app: IELTS Speaking and job-interview pronunciation trainer for Russian speakers
by_segment: Job seeker preparing an English interview (IT, outsourcing, international org)
Working professional needing IELTS for relocation or a master's
Student preparing IELTS to study abroad (family pays or part-time job)
by_behaviour: Already pays a course or tutor
why_not: Nobody in my IELTS Telegram chats has mentioned it yet, so I'd just use the free 3 fragments a day in the marshrutka and see if it actually works. Pronunciation alone isn't my main IELTS problem, so I won't pay for it on day one.

Nobody in my Telegram chats has mentioned this app yet, so I'd maybe try the free 3 fragments, but I won't pay. For an interview I worry more about what I say and my grammar than about single sounds, and this doesn't check that.

I already pay for an IELTS course, so I'd take the free 3 fragments a day and maybe the 7-day trial, then cancel before it charges. $4.99 a month on top of my course feels like one subscription too many.

I'd download it and use the 3 free fragments a day, maybe start the 7-day trial and cancel it before it charges, same as always. Between that, YouTube and ChatGPT voice I can practise for free, and I'm not spending my own $5 a month on pronunciation alone when it doesn't even check grammar or vocabulary.

I already pay my tutor and I only add apps she tells me to use. For an interview, pronunciation is not my real problem — what to say and grammar under pressure is, and ChatGPT voice mode does that for free. Maybe I'd use the 3 free fragments, but I wouldn't pay.

I already pay my tutor every month and she corrects my pronunciation in class, so another $5 on an app my teacher didn't suggest feels like wasted money. I'd maybe try the free 3 fragments a day, but I wouldn't pay for Pro.

My problem is that I freeze when I have to speak on my own, not that I mispronounce words, and reading a prepared text aloud doesn't fix that. I'd take the 7-day trial and then stay on the free 3 fragments a day, which fits into my evening plan anyway.
why_yes: My interview is in about three weeks and my accent is the thing I'm least sure of, so I'd run the free week hard and then pay for one month to get through to the interview date. After the interview I cancel.

I have an interview in a few weeks and I already practise every evening alone, so a daily plan with a countdown and a score for each sound fits how I work. I'd use the 7-day trial, and if it actually shows me progress I'd pay one month of $4.99 instead of the year.
My exam is in about three weeks, so I'd take the free 7 days, and if the Russian explanations actually show me which sounds I mess up, I'd pay for one month to get through the exam. Then I'd cancel.
